benchmarkValidation.conditionalIntervals: 95% pointwise intervals from 1,200 joint date block resamples within month, block 7, seed 20261108. Peer expectations are treated as fitted; not simultaneous intervals, causal effects or failure probabilities.
benchmarkValidation.diagnosticPolicy: Persistence requires at least four months below a benchmark plus a pointwise upper interval below 1. Economic review also requires above-median cost burden. Exploratory management screens, not multiplicity-adjusted defect tests. Fault Poisson flags use BH 5% but depend on a Poisson count assumption.
benchmarkValidation.benchmarkDecision: Retain exact leave-machine-out peer score for transparent location-conditional comparison. Add conditional intervals and expose cross-zone/temporal disagreement; fixed-support pooling is a sensitivity, not a selected empirical Bayes failure model.

manufacturerModel.method: Offset Poisson association adjusted for configuration, zone, month and weekday; quasi-Poisson dispersion interval. Observational, not a manufacturer treatment effect.

hourValidation.qualification: Quieter-hour scheduling estimates displaced opportunity only. It does not establish outage recovery or future demand. June profiles are planning bases, not held-out forecasts.

repeatRepairs.qualification: Time since prior repair is descriptive. Unrecorded condition and repeated tickets can confound preventive-treatment claims.

models.name: Zone×configuration and date fixed effects + Back Forty trend

closureDesign.method: Available-hour-weighted log wager-rate regression; zone×game-configuration and gaming-date fixed effects; Newey–West date-score covariance, lag 7. Date effects absorb shared weekday/calendar/event shifts. Trend specification is a sensitivity, not a causal repair.
closureDesign.limitations: Access was not randomized; local events, time-varying selection, spillovers and counter trends remain. No causal return assigned to signage or relocation.

payoutSensitivity.qualification: A constructed 0/a/max payout distribution matches RTP, hit probability and variance. Equal effective bets match aggregate first/second wager moments. It is not the actual unidentified paytable and need not respect every payout increment. Monte Carlo error interval covers this simulation only. It is a sensitivity check, not a replacement p-value or defect probability.

forecastResearch.decision: Keep the original April-selected weekday mean for the headline frozen evaluation. New February–April rolling-origin and nested ridge diagnostics are retrospective model research, not a newly untouched final test.
forecastResearch.fairness: All models receive the same information before each origin and predict the full following month without using observations from that month. Seasonal naive repeats the last available weekday cycle; it does not consume future actual lags.

medianVsMeanMaeDifference.qualification: Paired, month-stratified circular block resampling of retrospective rolling-origin errors. Not an untouched external test or a causal scheduling benefit.

qualifications: New diagnostics are retrospective/exploratory; no causal treatment effect or new untouched holdout is claimed.
Contribution includes only supplied costs and is not complete profit.
Conditional pointwise peer intervals do not estimate intrinsic machine defects or simultaneous failure probabilities.

opportunities.evidence: 680 faults over 16839 active machine-days; adjusted rate ratio 3.56 versus Halcyon.

base.scheduleMode: June quiet-hour proxy; at most one target job per eligible day assumed

opportunities.uncertainty: Rate-ratio interval is model-based; repeat tickets and unmeasured condition can confound association.
opportunities.causal: Inspection can identify a cause; preventive and staffing recoveries are unobserved.
opportunities.priority: Investigate recurring faults before a broad sweep

opportunities.title: Access and location demand opportunity
opportunities.scaleLabel: June-based 20-day zone theo baseline (not recoverable loss)
opportunities.strength: Repeated rate pattern + comparative historical design
opportunities.uncertainty: Pre-trends differ and local confounding remains; ranks depend strongly on benchmark geography.
opportunities.causal: No causal signage or relocation uplift is identified. Property-wide displacement must be measured.

measurement.primary: Incremental property-wide theo/contribution after supplied incremental costs, adjusted for available hours and calendar
measurement.secondary: Zone wager rate, crossings per covered sensor-hour, occupancy and displacement to/from other zones
measurement.baseline: Pre-register June 11–30 and a matched weekday/control comparison before work
measurement.stop: Freeze analysis before launch; inspect weekly operational harm, stop if demand shifts away elsewhere or signs impair access. A small break-even effect may be undetectable in 20 days; inconclusive evidence does not prove zero.

opportunities.title: Point-price change warrants a controlled policy test
opportunities.evidence: Recorded May point-price shift persists with fixed item×tier mix; supported cells cover 98.93% of January face value.
opportunities.uncertainty: Behavioral response, unused point liability and uncarded activity are not identified.
opportunities.causal: No causal policy benefit is booked; information value is unpriced.
opportunities.priority: Test before a floor-wide rate change

opportunities.evidence: Supplied costs are 41.2% of theo; all machines remain positive on six-month contribution after supplied costs.

base.scheduleMode: June quiet-hour proxy; at most one target job per eligible day assumed

opportunities.uncertainty: Contract termination savings, new-title demand and full overhead are absent. No avoided old lease cost is silently credited.
opportunities.causal: Replacing a positive-contribution machine needs an incremental business case.

measurement.primary: Incremental contribution versus retained matched machines
measurement.baseline: June active-machine contribution and actual cost terms
measurement.period: 16 eligible lease days or nine purchase days; long-run asset value outside this horizon
measurement.stop: Do not replace solely on raw win or a descriptive percentile.

opportunities.title: Queue opportunity is smaller than full downtime
opportunities.evidence: 1377.8 queued hours intersect metered outages; hands-on repair is a different process.
opportunities.scaleLabel: Six-month queue theo proxy (not causal recovery)
opportunities.uncertainty: Adding a technician cannot recover all repair time; guests may switch machines.
opportunities.causal: The recoverable fraction is a scenario and capped at its shift pool.
opportunities.priority: Compare full-recovery ceiling with cost before staffing

measurement.primary: Metered queued downtime by shift and property-wide contribution
measurement.control: Comparable shifts/weeks; record actual staffing and queue arrivals
measurement.stop: Do not add ticket durations to metered downtime or count the same recovery twice.

opportunities.title: Schedule work in lower-demand hours
opportunities.evidence: Observed theo per available hour 3.21 versus 33.28. Frozen training-window quiet choice remains best in the later diagnostic.
opportunities.scaleLabel: Observed hourly theo-rate difference per machine
opportunities.uncertainty: June profiles are planning proxies; July demand and scheduling constraints can differ.
opportunities.causal: Moving planned work in time does not create new play or guarantee recovered profit.
opportunities.priority: Use as a scheduling condition on every action

measurement.primary: Actual scheduled start, downtime and displaced play
measurement.period: Every intervention; gaming-day boundary and guest-access constraints respected
measurement.stop: Reconcile actual outage to meters; do not claim the debit difference as observed earnings.

search.scope: Exhaustive combinations of generated evidence-based bundles, not all possible machine/location/quantity configurations. Preserve cash is included.

scenarioAssumptions.rates: Explicit low/base/high effects by action; no effect probabilities or causal estimates.
scenarioAssumptions.displacement: Positive demand base retains 50%, high retains 75%; low negative effects are not reduced.
scenarioAssumptions.costs: Catalog costs charged in full; quiet-window debit uses June hourly theo profiles; no unverified old-contract savings.
scenarioAssumptions.overlap: Largest positive benefit in each demand/recovery pool, all negative effects counted.

objectives.financial: Maximize base-scenario incremental property-wide contribution after catalog costs, opportunity debit, displacement and overlap; ties favor higher low-scenario net, then lower spend. Base effects are explicit assumptions, not estimated causal returns.
objectives.riskSensitive: Maximize the same base-scenario net subject to the stated low-scenario downside cap. The cap is a management preference, not a learned parameter or probabilistic guarantee.
objectives.robust: Maximize low-scenario net (maximin), then prefer lower spend; robustness covers the declared scenarios only.
objectives.learning: Maximize distinct pre-registered questions under the stated downside cap, then base-scenario net and lower spend. Information value is unpriced; this objective can accept negative financial results.

monitoringPlan.monitor: Review existing ticket logs weekly: faults per active machine-day, queue wait intersecting meter downtime, hands-on hours and direct repair costs.
monitoringPlan.trigger: Approve paid repair/inspection only with a documented recoverable cause and credible avoided property contribution above catalog cost plus downtime debit, or explicitly choose the experimental objective. A manufacturer association alone is insufficient.

monitoringPlan.monitor: Continue routine meter/configuration reconciliation; retain the full testing-family qualification. A residual is not a defect diagnosis.
monitoringPlan.trigger: A verified configuration discrepancy or documented exposure changes the business case. A paid catalog inspection remains separately priced; it is not silently included as free work.

monitoringPlan.monitor: Track wager/theo per available hour, occupancy and crossings per covered sensor-hour alongside other zones and property totals; compare weekdays and game mix.
monitoringPlan.trigger: Fund wayfinding only when credible incremental property contribution clears its displayed break-even threshold after displacement and the 10-day lead, or opt into controlled learning. The closure association is not a signage effect estimate.

monitoringPlan.monitor: Reconcile weekly redeemed economic cost, points per fixed item/tier face value, tracked outcomes and property contribution. Protect guests; do not optimize losses of vulnerable cohorts.
monitoringPlan.trigger: Fund a point-rate change only with credible net incremental contribution above its break-even boundary and harm controls. A controlled $4,000 pilot belongs to the optional experimental budget; reduced points per face dollar alone proves no behavioral uplift.

monitoringPlan.monitor: Review exposure-adjusted demand, contribution after supplied costs and availability before any ten-machine order. Use the frozen weekday model for demand/scheduling context, not treatment ROI.
monitoringPlan.trigger: Require prospective replacement benefit above full lease/purchase cost and outage opportunity, with exact eligible days and property-wide displacement. Ten purchases remain infeasible; re-run the financial search when verified inputs or explicit assumptions change.
